jobs.title: Head of Marketing
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Rebar

Rebar is building the AI operating system for commercial HVAC, Electrical, and Plumbing.

Over the past year our quoting platform has processed tens of thousands of projects across North America and we’ve doubled our revenue in the first 6 weeks of this year. Our customers include many of the top firms in the industry. Some of these companies are running billion-dollar construction projects on workflows that still look like it’s 1985.

Construction is 10% of GDP and still massively underserved by software. We are changing that.

We recently raised a $14M Series A from leading construction tech investors and are entering our next phase of growth. We are building a set of AI native products that will define how this industry operates.

We’re looking for a Head of Marketing to build and lead Rebar’s marketing function—driving pipeline, sharpening our positioning, and defining how we show up in the market.

The Role

We're hiring a Head of Marketing to own Rebar's marketing function end-to-end: strategy, budget, demand generation, brand, content, events, and positioning. You'll build the team that runs it as we scale. We believe the commercial construction supply chain is about to go through a massive AI-driven transformation. Rebar sits at the center of that shift, and we have a unique opportunity to become the defining voice of AI in pre-construction.

This is our first marketing leadership hire, and it's a player-coach role. You'll set the strategy and own the number, and you'll also write the posts, launch the campaigns, and work with our events team. You'll report to the CEO, work closely with the Head of Sales, and be part of the leadership team shaping company strategy.

Today, much of our growth comes from strong market pull, customer referrals, industry relationships, and outbound sales. You'll own Rebar's external presence: how we show up across every channel and every room. That means the content that earns trust, the events where relationships get built, and the commercial narrative that makes us the obvious call before a demo is even scheduled.

What You'll Do

Own Marketing Strategy & Build the Team

  • Set Rebar's marketing strategy, annual plan, and budget, tied directly to pipeline and revenue targets

  • Own the marketing-sourced pipeline number and report on it to the CEO, the leadership team, and the board

  • Build and scale demand generation across paid acquisition, lifecycle, outbound campaigns, partnerships, events, and growth experiments

  • Run performance marketing end-to-end on channels like LinkedIn and Google Ads, including audience strategy, creative, landing pages, and attribution

  • Improve conversion across the funnel through messaging, targeting, experimentation, and optimization

  • Hire and develop the marketing team as we scale. Decide when to hire full-time and when to use contractors or agencies, and manage those partners across paid, design, video, and content

Define Rebar's Voice in the Market

  • Establish Rebar as the defining voice of AI in pre-construction and commercial construction supply

  • Own Rebar's LinkedIn presence across organic and paid. Ship consistent, high-quality content, including customer stories, product launches, podcast clips, executive POVs, and industry commentary

  • Build a scalable content engine across thought leadership, product marketing, newsletters, webinars, sales enablement, and educational content for suppliers, estimators, contractors, and operators

  • Turn customer pain points, workflows, and product capabilities into clear, compelling messaging that lands with commercial construction teams

  • Partner with the CEO on a founder-led content program. The CEO commits about 2 hours a week to content collaboration (interviews, raw audio, draft reviews) and shows up for the podcast

Build Customer & Industry Storytelling

  • Stand up and scale Rebar's customer story and testimonial engine from sourcing and interviews through approvals, publishing, and multi-format distribution

  • Create high-quality marketing assets that support both brand building and pipeline generation, including case studies, one-pagers, decks, launch materials, demo collateral, and sales enablement content

  • Launch and scale Rebar's webinar and podcast initiatives across both live and on-demand formats

Lead Strategic GTM & Partnerships

  • Choose which conferences, trade shows, sponsorships, and industry partnerships to invest in based on our ICP, and own the event budget and ROI

  • Enable strategic partners with co-branded campaigns, collateral, and partner toolkits

  • Partner closely with Sales, Product, and Leadership on GTM strategy, product launches, roadmap communication, and market positioning. With Sales, that means a weekly pipeline review with the Head of Sales, a shared dashboard for marketing-sourced vs. influenced pipeline, and joint ownership of the named account list

Measure and Optimize Performance

  • Own marketing's metrics: attribution, pipeline influence, CAC efficiency, and funnel conversion

  • Run rapid experiments across channels, messaging, creative, and targeting to find what works and scale it

What We're Looking For

The non-negotiables, written through the lens of how this role will partner with Sales:

  • 6+ years in B2B SaaS marketing, demand generation, growth, or GTM roles, including at least 2 years leading a marketing function or team, ideally at an early-stage company. You've built something from zero, not only inherited it.

  • You've carried a real pipeline number. Not "supported pipeline." You've owned a marketing-sourced target, missed it, made it back, and can walk us through what worked. If you've never been on the hook for revenue, you'll default to brand work when it gets uncomfortable.

  • You've built and led a team. You've hired marketers, managed agencies, and know when to hire versus buy. You still do the work yourself; you can lead without stepping away from execution.

  • You'll get on customer calls. You work in Attention, sit on live calls, listen to losses, and talk to estimators on the phone. You don't build from a deck or an analyst report. Without this, voice and positioning will be wrong within 60 days.

  • You speak practitioner, not marketer. You can write for a 55-year-old distributor branch manager. Our ICP can smell SaaS marketing copy from a mile away. Expect a writing exercise in the loop: 20 minutes of raw CEO audio in, polished post out.

  • ABM in execution, not on slides. You've run 1:1, 1:few, and 1:many programs with an SDR team and adjusted plays in flight. You know the difference between intent data that's useful and intent data that's noise. You've fought through bad attribution and built something better.

  • Event-led pipeline ops. Pre-event outreach cadence, dinners, booth playbook, post-event handoff to sales. This is where marketing either earns its seat or doesn't.

  • You ship sales enablement on request. One-pager by Tuesday, case study in a week. No "that's a Q3 OKR" energy. You bring a service mindset to the deal team, and in return the sales team brings the same mindset to you.

  • Closed-lost obsession. You read every loss reason and feed it back into positioning. Most marketers ignore lost deals, but that's where messaging actually gets sharp.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary: $200k-$350k

  • Equity: meaningful grant, aligned with your background

  • Benefits: medical, dental, vision

  • Perks: free lunches and dinners

This is a full-time, onsite role in NYC’s Flatiron District—steps from Madison Square Park and Union Square.

We are looking for our next Account Executive who wants to move fast and take ownership early. You will help define how AI changes one of the largest industries in the world.

As an early Account Executive at Rebar you’ll pair real selling craft with a builder's mindset, partnering directly with our founders and serving as the bridge between customers and product.

Drive revenue and customer growth

  • Own the full sales cycle: prospecting, demos, follow-ups, pricing, and close

  • Run live demos that prove the product on the customer's own drawings

  • Develop relationships across HVAC, electrical, and plumbing reps, contractors, and distributors

  • Provide feedback to leadership on pricing, product positioning, and GTM strategy

Become the voice of the customer

  • Understand the takeoff, estimating, and quoting workflows better than anyone

  • Turn customer pain points into clear product requirements

  • Work closely with product and engineering to help shape the roadmap

  • Serve as a thought partner to the founders on positioning and pricing

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 3–10+ years selling complex, workflow-heavy products, with a proven track record of closing

  • Comfortable running high-trust, multi-call, multi-stakeholder sales cycles

  • Credibility with skeptical, operator-led buyers, you can hold the room and earn trust fast

  • Genuine appetite to go deep on the trade: takeoffs, estimating, and quoting workflows

  • Comfortable in early-stage environments: scrappy, creative, and fast

  • Exceptional communication and customer-facing skills

Strong plus (shortens your ramp)

  • Experience selling into HVAC, electrical, or plumbing from the trades side or the software side

  • Worked in construction and then moved into construction-tech

  • Understanding of mechanical drawings, equipment schedules, and plan sets

Compensation and Benefits

  • Salary: Competitive base and OTE

  • Equity: meaningful grant, aligned with your background

  • Benefits: medical, dental, vision

  • Perks: free lunches and dinners

Strategic Account Executive, Manufacturer Partnerships

About Rebar

Rebar is building the AI operating system for commercial HVAC, Electrical, and Plumbing.

Over the past year our quoting platform has processed tens of thousands of projects across North America and we’ve doubled our revenue in the first 6 weeks of this year. Our customers include many of the top firms in the industry. Some of these companies are running billion-dollar construction projects on workflows that still look like it’s 1985.

Construction is 10% of GDP and still massively underserved by software. We are changing that.

We recently raised a $14M Series A from leading construction tech investors and are entering our next phase of growth. We are building a set of AI native products that will define how this industry operates.

We’re looking for someone to build and own our manufacturer partnerships business—developing the strategy, opening the right doors, and defining how Rebar partners with manufacturers.

The Role

Today, Rebar sells to the people who bid the work: manufacturer reps, distributors, and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing contractors. The next step is building direct partnerships with the manufacturers whose products our customers sell and install.

There are two core parts of this role:

  1. Build manufacturer partnerships. Develop relationships with manufacturers to bring their product selection and pricing information directly into Rebar, making it easier for our customers to specify, select, and quote their products.

  2. Sell market intelligence. Rebar processes thousands of plans and specs, giving us unique visibility into what products are being specified and bid, where projects are happening, and how the market is moving. You will work with manufacturers to turn this data into a valuable market intelligence product that competes directly with platforms like Dodge.

As the Strategic AE for Manufacturer Partnerships, you will own both motions from the ground up. You’ll identify the right manufacturers and decision-makers, open doors, determine the right commercial model, and close our first partnerships.

We’re looking for someone who already comes from this world. You understand how manufacturers operate, know the people who make these decisions, and bring existing relationships that can open doors from day one. We’re not looking for someone to learn the industry—we’re looking for someone who already knows it and can help us build the business within it.

You Will

Build the point of view, then the plan

  • Spend your first 90 days in conversation with the market, and come back with findings rather than a pitch: which manufacturers, which product and equipment categories, which people inside them, and what each would value

  • Turn those findings into a written partnership strategy: target list, entry point, offer, and pricing, with the reasoning behind each call

  • Be honest about what you learn, including where the opportunity is smaller or slower than we hoped

Design how our manufacturer relationships are formed

  • Work out the commercial model with us as you learn more about the market. Manufacturers might pay for market intelligence drawn from the projects we see, for takeoff capacity, for business generated through Rebar, or for a model nobody in this space has tried yet. We have hypotheses, not answers

  • Pressure-test each model against how manufacturers actually budget and buy, including their purchasing and procurement process

Open and close the first partnerships

  • Use your existing manufacturer relationships to get the right conversations started quickly

  • Run the full sale: from first meeting through procurement, legal, and signature

  • Build relationships at the level where partnership decisions get made, not only with the territory or channel contact

Shape the product

  • Tell our product team what would make a manufacturer partnership work: the integrations, data, and capabilities a manufacturer would need before they sign

  • Find out which manufacturers do takeoffs themselves today, how, and what that work costs them

  • Bring every signal back as evidence from real conversations, so product decisions rest on what manufacturers said rather than what we assumed

What We're Looking For

Required

  • Deep, current relationships with US manufacturers in commercial HVAC, mechanical, electrical, or plumbing equipment, strong enough that the right people will take your call this year

  • Breadth across manufacturers and categories. Experience that spans several manufacturers and several product or equipment categories, rather than one manufacturer's line in one territory. A long career at a rep agency carrying multiple lines is exactly the kind of background we have in mind

  • You know how manufacturers buy. You understand their purchasing and procurement process, who holds budget, and how a new vendor or partner gets approved

  • Strategic and creative about monetization. You have sold, structured, or priced something that did not come with a rate card, and can walk us through how you landed on the number

  • Independent. You are comfortable shaping the approach yourself, testing it in the market, and changing course when the evidence says to

  • A senior track record of closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals where the buyer had to be convinced the category was worth paying for at all

  • Comfortable in early-stage environments: scrappy, creative, and fast

  • Exceptional communication with operators and executives in the trades

Strong plus

  • Experience in construction data or project-intelligence businesses, and an understanding of how manufacturers use project and specification data today

  • Has built a partnership, channel, or data-licensing program from scratch

  • Has worked closely with a product team to turn customer conversations into what gets built

Compensation and Benefits

  • Compensation. Competitive based on experience

  • Equity: meaningful grant, aligned with your background

  • Benefits: medical, dental, vision

This a fully remote role, with 30%+ travel.

THE ROLE

We're hiring our first Revenue Operations Lead to own the operating system behind Rebar's revenue engine: Marketing, Sales Development, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance, along with the systems, processes, data, and planning that connects them.

Today each team runs its own tools, keeping their own version of the truth. Marketing runs events and field programs that need to land in the CRM with a source attached. Sales needs a forecast it can trust. Customer Success needs clean accounts and renewal triggers. Finance needs every contract and every dollar of ARR change to live in one place. You'll be the connective tissue between them, and the test of the role is simple: one number that agrees everywhere it appears.

This is a hands-on seat. You'll be the first and only person in the function, working with the Head of Sales, Head of CS, Finance, Marketing, and our GTM Engineer, who builds the automation and data pipelines that feed the CRM. You own the system of record, the definitions, and the process. We're at the point where the foundations are being built, cleaning up what exists today and designing what we need to scale.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Rebar

Rebar is building the AI operating system for commercial HVAC, Electrical, and Plumbing.

Commercial mechanical, electrical, and plumbing firms run billion-dollar construction projects on workflows that still look like it’s 1985.

Construction is 10% of GDP and still massively underserved by software. We are changing that.

We recently raised a $14M Series A from leading construction tech investors and are entering our next phase of growth. We are building a set of AI native products that will define how this industry operates.

We are looking for a Business Development Representative (BDR) who wants to build, move fast, and take ownership early. You will help define how AI changes one of the largest industries in the world.

The Role

As a BDR at Rebar, you own the front door of revenue: finding the right prospects across HVAC, electrical, and plumbing, and booking qualified meetings directly onto Account Executives' calendars. Our growth depends on a steady stream of the right people getting into the right conversations, and you're the one making that happen every day on the phone.

You'll run Rebar's proven cold-open playbook, qualify hard before you book, and hand off clean, well-documented meetings that set the AE up to win. The ramp is fast: you'll be booking real meetings in your first few weeks. And this isn't a dead-end seat. BDRs who perform have a real, defined path to Account Executive.

You Will

Find, qualify, and book

  • Work a pre-built, enriched calling queue (list-building and enrichment are handled upstream, so you spend your time dialing, not sourcing)

  • Run real discovery on the first call instead of a scripted pitch, and qualify prospects against a clear, defined bar before booking anything

  • Book qualified meetings directly onto Account Executive calendars, with clean handoff notes so the AE walks in already oriented

  • Log every call outcome accurately: your dispositions feed the pipeline directly and become a live signal into the product roadmap

Learn the trade and specialize

  • Ramp on a shared foundation covering every segment we sell into, then go deep on one (mechanical, electrical, or distribution)

  • Build real fluency in how commercial HVAC, electrical, and plumbing shops actually operate, no prior trade background required

  • Get coached weekly on your actual calls: openers, objection handling, qualification discipline

Move the number

  • Own a monthly qualified-meeting quota that ramps over your first few months

  • Work inside one live dialer as your system of record; no side spreadsheets, no manual pipeline upkeep

  • Turn a "not now" into a real re-engagement opportunity instead of a dead lead

What We're Looking For

Required

  • Real cold-calling or outbound experience, in any industry; comfortable with high call volume and frequent rejection

  • Resilient: doesn't fold at the first brush-off, stays genuinely curious about what's actually going on with a prospect

  • Coachable: takes direct, specific feedback on call technique and applies it immediately

  • Comfortable in early-stage environments: scrappy, creative, and fast

  • Exceptional verbal communication; builds rapport and credibility fast with a skeptical, operator-led buyer

Strong plus (shortens your ramp)

  • Prior BDR/SDR experience at a B2B SaaS or workflow-software company

  • Experience selling or working in HVAC, electrical, plumbing, or an adjacent trades/construction segment

  • Familiarity with a modern dialer (Nooks, Hubspot, or similar)

  • Worked in construction and then moved into sales or construction-tech

Compensation and Benefits

  • Salary: competitive base + per-meeting bonus

  • Equity: meaningful grant, aligned with your background

  • Benefits: medical, dental, vision

  • Perks: free lunches and dinners

This is a full-time, onsite role in NYC's Flatiron District, steps from Madison Square Park and Union Square.

About Rebar

Rebar is building the AI operating system for commercial HVAC, Electrical, and Plumbing.

Some of these companies are running billion dollar construction projects on workflows that still look like it's 1985.

Construction is 10% of GDP and still massively underserved by software. We are changing that.

We recently raised a $14M Series A from leading construction tech investors and are entering our next phase of growth. We are building a set of AI native products that will define how this industry operates.

About the Engineering Org

The role of the engineer is rapidly changing. We're aware and we're being very intentional of ensuring we adapt with it. We are fostering an engineering culture of growth and development. We strongly emphasize care of craft and winning together. To echo our values, everyone operates like an owner, we find a way, and we win together.

About the Role

This role is going to be sitting on our AI and ML team as a backend engineer.

You will be working directly with our in house models (as well as frontier VLMs) so that we can build a world class interaction for the frontend. For example, you could be taking a segmentation mask that one of our detection models produces, deciding what it should become on the canvas - a polygon, a polyline, a set of connection ports - designing the contract that carries it there, and then making it something our users can grab and correct.

The job is not just "make the model better", it’s to have the ideal shape and use case for the user can see, trust, correct, and bill against.

Responsibilities

  • Design the perception → product data contract

  • Ship AI geometry into the canvas

  • Own the accuracy and UX tradeoff honestly

  • Close the correction loop

  • Be the translation layer between our AI/ML team and the product engineers

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone comfortable working largely across the stack. You should be comfortable reading a PyTorch postprocessing path in the morning and then understanding the flow to the canvas rendering path in the afternoon. You should be willing to dive deeper into understand model architectures and spotting inefficiencies as their outputs are translated downstream.

Qualifications

  • 6+ years of industry software engineering experience

    • If fewer than 6 years of experience, still encouraged to apply!

  • Shipped computer vision or ML output into a product surface that users interact with daily

  • Comfortable in Python and TypeScript

  • Experience designing and versioning data contracts between services on live customer data

Nice to Have

  • Canvas and rendering experience

  • Familiarity with vector graphic object models, standards, and protocols

  • Experience building human in the loop labeling or active learning loops

  • Construction, CAD, GIS, or another domain where drawings are the source of truth

Compensation and Benefits

  • Salary: Competitive base salary

  • Equity: Meaningful equity package, commensurate with experience

  • Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

  • Perks:

    • Agentic tooling budget

    • Lunches provided, dinners provided (after a set time)

    • Great culture and office banter

This is a salaried, onsite role located in New York City's Flatiron district. We are still a startup! We love working onsite together and believe strongly that this gives us for creative problem-solving, and building strong connections. You'll be at the heart of our fast-paced operations, actively contributing to a culture that values engagement, growth, and teamwork.

  • We win together

That being said the whole company still works really hard! This is something that you should read and internalize. This might not be the place for everyone.

About the Role

We're looking for a Software Engineer focused on our product. This hire will own the engineering behind key product expansion, a quickly rising quality bar, and the architecture of the application our customers live in all day.

Our product engineers are full stack with a slight frontend skew. While numerous difficult customer workflows and interactions sit in the client, you'll still ship and own features end to end. You should be comfortable in DBeaver with Postgres or digging into the React profiler.

Our product is a browser-based (konva) canvas editor on top of extremely dense construction drawings. Estimators open a planset with thousands of pages, our models mark it up, and multiple people edit the same document at the same time. That means the hard problems here are not CRUD screens. They are rendering performance on enormous documents, correctness in a collaborative document, and state that has to survive a flaky jobsite network.

This is a scale moment for us. We are expanding both vertically up our market as well as branching into new markets like hydronics and plumbing. We need an experienced and technically strong engineer to help us accomplish that.

I cannot state this enough - I will personally ensure that you leave as a better and more experienced engineer than when you joined. You will get to set the technical standard for a product org as it roughly doubles over the next year, own a genuinely hard piece of client-side engineering, and watch it scale fr om hundreds of companies to thousands.

Responsibilities

  • Own runtime quality of the product

    • Interaction latency, rendering performance, memory, and correctness on real customer projects - not lab conditions. You own the metrics, the budgets, and the regressions.

  • Own the hard client-side architecture

    • The canvas editor, the collaborative document layer, and the state that ties them together.

  • Help set a strong engineering standard in the agentic world

    • Help continue to raise the quality bar for the engineering org

  • Raise the review and testing bar

    • Required checks, meaningful end-to-end coverage of the flows that actually break, and review that catches design problems rather than typos.

  • Ship features end to end

    • From the editor down through the API and the database. You design the data model and the endpoints your feature needs rather than waiting on someone else to build them.

What We’re Looking For

At a high level, we want technical depth plus the taste to know what not to build. You should actually give a shit about how the product feels under a user's hands.

You should be able to walk me through the last time you took a slow, heavy interface and made it fast - what you profiled, what you measured, what you shipped, and what you deliberately left alone. You should have opinions about testing that come from having been burned. In addition, we’re asking for comfort across the whole stack, so that you’re excited and eager to jump into our collaboration engine and understand data flow end to end.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years building production web applications, with significant time in a large, long-lived codebase

  • Deep React and TypeScript - you know how rendering actually works and you can reason about it without guessing

  • Real browser performance work: profiling, interaction latency, memory, rendering

  • Has owned complex client-side state in production - not just fetch and render

  • Solid backend fundamentals: you've designed APIs and relational data models, written migrations, and run server-side code in production (we're Python and Postgres on AWS and GCP)

  • Comfortable owning a domain end to end, including the production incidents in it

Nice to Have

  • Canvas or WebGL rendering at scale (Konva, Pixi, Three, custom) - we're on Konva today and evaluating a move

  • Real-time collaboration and CRDTs (Yjs, Automerge, ShareDB), and the failure modes that come with them

  • Offline and unreliable-network handling: IndexedDB, local persistence, reconnect and conflict behavior

  • Backend depth beyond CRUD: Postgres query and schema performance, durable async workflows (we use Temporal), or the server side of a real-time system

Compensation and Benefits

  • Salary: Competitive base salary

  • Equity: Meaningful equity package, commensurate with experience

  • Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

  • Perks:

    • agentic tooling budget

    • lunches provided, dinners provided (after a set time)

    • great culture and office banter

This is a salaried, onsite role located in New York City's Flatiron district. We are still a startup! We love working onsite together and believe strongly that this gives us creative problem-solving, and building strong connections.

  • Engage regularly with customers to understand workflows and pain points

  • Identify and prioritize high-impact problems to solve

  • Improve and expand the core product experience

  • Contribute to launching new products and features

  • Turn customer feedback into clear, actionable product direction

  • Help build and refine how we plan and ship product

  • Collaborate with engineering and design to iterate quickly and deliver high-quality work

  • Support alignment across customer and internal feedback

About Rebar

Rebar is building the AI operating system for commercial HVAC, Electrical, and Plumbing.

Over the past year, our quoting platform has processed tens of thousands of projects across North America, and we’ve doubled our revenue in the first 6 weeks of this year. Our customers include many of the top firms in the industry. Some of these companies are running billion-dollar construction projects on workflows that still look like it’s 1985.

Construction is 10% of GDP and still massively underserved by software. We are changing that.

We recently raised a $14M Series A from leading construction tech investors and are entering our next phase of growth. We are building a set of AI native products that will define how this industry operates.

We are looking for a Manager of Technical Support who wants to build a support team clients rave about. Our clients already tell each other that Rebar support is one of the best reasons to work with us, and your job is to scale that as we grow. You will lead and expand our technical support team, extend coverage to serve customers in every US time zone, and build the processes, tooling, and metrics that keep us fast and human at higher volume. You will partner with Product and Engineering to turn support insights into product improvements, making sure what clients experience shapes how we bring AI to construction.

About the Role

We aren't a call center. We respond fast, we're human, and we go the extra mile for every client. The foundation is solid, and our customer base is growing quickly. We need a leader to scale the team and its processes without losing what makes our support special.

Reporting directly to the Head of Client Success, you'll lead and grow our team of two remote Technical Support Specialists into a team that covers the whole country. Today we cover 7 a.m.–8 p.m. ET. With clients across the US, including Alaska and Hawaii, we need to extend coverage through 7 p.m. PT (10 p.m. ET). We're looking to you to build the team, structure, and technical depth to make that happen.

What You'll Do

  • Build and scale the team: hire, onboard, and develop Technical Support Specialists as we expand from Eastern-heavy coverage to nationwide coverage through 7 p.m. PT.

  • Design coverage models: create staffing plans, schedules, and shift structures that keep response times fast across every US time zone.

  • Lead and coach: run 1:1s, give regular feedback, and set clear expectations so each specialist grows their technical skills and their career.

  • Own support performance: set, track, and report on SLAs and KPIs (first response time, resolution time, CSAT, backlog, and escalation rate), and hold the team to a high standard.

  • Protect the client experience: keep support personal, proactive, and human as volume grows. Speed matters, and so does going the extra mile.

  • Shape AI-assisted support: decide how Intercom Fin and AI workflows handle routine questions so your team can focus on the problems that need a person.

  • Build processes and structure: create and refine the workflows, escalation paths, triage rules, macros, and playbooks that let the team scale.

  • Own our support tooling: manage and improve our Intercom setup (inbox routing, automations, help center and reporting) and its integrations with HubSpot, Linear and other internal tools.

  • Develop technical expertise: build training programs so the team knows our product, construction and MEP (mechanical, electrical and plumbing) workflows, and troubleshooting inside out.

  • Partner with Engineering and Product: bring bugs, trends and product gaps to the right people with clear, prioritized, data-backed feedback, and push complex issues through to resolution.

  • Collaborate with Client Success and Implementation: keep handoffs smooth across the client journey, and share insights on account health, adoption risk and upsell signals.

  • Stay hands-on: jump into the queue, take escalations and lead by example when it counts.

What You Bring

  • 5+ years in technical support for B2B SaaS, including 2+ years managing or leading a support team

  • A track record of building a support function from scratch or scaling one through rapid growth, including its processes, SLAs, escalation workflows, and team structure

  • Strong troubleshooting skills with web-based software, and the ability to coach others on them

  • Experience hiring, coaching, and retaining high-performing remote team members

  • Comfort using data to manage performance, spot trends, and make staffing decisions

  • Clear communication with clients, your team and cross-functional partners, technical and non-technical alike, and a belief that great support is a competitive advantage, not a cost center

Bonus

  • Hands-on Intercom experience (strongly preferred), including admin, automations, Fin, help center, and reporting

  • Background in construction, construction tech, or MEP contracting

  • Experience at an early-stage or high-growth startup

  • Experience designing coverage models across multiple time zones

  • Familiarity with APIs, integrations, or debugging tools

  • Experience with Linear, Jira, HubSpot, Slack, or similar tools

  • Experience building knowledge bases, training programs, and client-facing documentation

If you meet most of these but not all, we still want to hear from you!

What Success Looks Like

First 30 days

  • Learn the product, client segments, workflows, and common support issues hands-on, and become a product expert

  • Work the queue alongside the team to understand how support runs today

  • Build relationships with Client Success, Implementation, Product, and Engineering

  • Audit current processes, SLAs, Intercom setup and reporting, and identify gaps and quick wins

  • Set up a regular 1:1 and coaching cadence with each specialist

First 60 days

  • Deliver a coverage plan and hiring roadmap to reach nationwide coverage through 7 p.m. PT

  • Put core KPIs and a recurring support performance report in place

  • Ship the first set of process improvements (triage, escalation paths, macros and documentation)

First 90 days

  • Start hiring against the coverage plan, with an onboarding and training program ready

  • Build a repeatable technical training path for new and current specialists

  • Hold or improve first response time and CSAT while volume grows

  • Run a consistent feedback loop with Product and Engineering on recurring issues and product gaps

Compensation and Benefits

  • Base salary: 120,000-145,000 USD per year. The final offer depends on experience and skills.

  • Equity: a meaningful grant, aligned with your background

  • Health: medical, dental, and vision

  • Unlimited PTO, team lunches

Location

This is a full-time, onsite role in NYC's Flatiron District, steps from Madison Square Park and Union Square. You'll work side by side with a high-performing team, solve real problems in real time, and help shape the future of an industry AI hasn't reached yet.

Equal Opportunity

Rebar is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.
